lessons: Use an external original-research page as a lead, and test its claimed callback locally with a strictly allowing passive recorder before relying on availability.

This pinned vanilla runtime emitted player/fullunitID/operationIndex for both a true FOUND qualification and a false SKIP qualification. The callback is therefore not a submitted/accepted/completed request receipt.
The observed callback has three arguments and no requestID/token. It cannot alone distinguish a delayed old request from a new replay or establish a global inbound queue barrier.

Read qualification, SDK writer submission, raw operation events, independent state and journal outcome as separate evidence layers. Here two qualification callbacks occurred with zero observed target SDK requests and zero target raw operation events.

Do not stop at safe refusal. Complete same-prefix logs showed unknown-owner and unknown-formation refusal lacked a current-turn reason, even though the qualifier-recovery subcases succeeded. Fix the product explanation gap instead of declaring the whole case passed.
Keep callback prototype tests in one Lua VM per witness. Mixing objects from different runtimes is a test harness failure, not a game failure.
